label: PF Backlog 640
title: Hard-gate the review lifecycle: Gate 1.5 -> Gate 1 before work, Gate 2.5 -> Gate 2 before completion
body: Today only Gate 2.5 is mechanically enforced. Gate 1 is bypassable by never moving an item to in_progress (items can go new->completed), and Gate 2/HIL delivery approval is not recorded or checked. Make all four gates hard for every backlog item.

decisions.note: Gate 1: user directive that all four gates are hard. Gate 1.5 findings dispositioned (0 pending); design constraints recorded.
Gate 1: user directive to hard-gate all four review gates; Gate 1.5 findings dispositioned (0 pending). Residual: approver identity is procedural, not signed.

brief.problem: Today only Gate 2.5 is mechanically enforced. Gate 1 is bypassable by never moving an item to in_progress (items can go new->completed), and Gate 2/HIL delivery approval is not recorded or checked. Make all four gates hard for every backlog item.
brief.what_adds: Hard-gate the review lifecycle: Gate 1.5 -> Gate 1 before work, Gate 2.5 -> Gate 2 before completion
brief.why: Today only Gate 2.5 is mechanically enforced. Gate 1 is bypassable by never moving an item to in_progress (items can go new->completed), and Gate 2/HIL delivery approval is not recorded or checked. Make all four gates hard for every backlog item.

objective: Hard gates for every item with deterministic, testable predicates: design-sha binding, decision ordering, fail-closed baseline/expiry, shared predicates, git-audited force, and explicit ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Gate 1.5 (design evidence) is mandatory for every item transitioning new->in_progress in the committed diff: reusable gate1_check.evaluate must return parseable evidence with zero PENDING BLOCKER/MAJOR (grandfathering removed; legacy items are untouched unless they transition).

Gate 1 (HIL design approval) is mandatory before implementation: a decision {gate:1, decision:APPROVE|APPROVE_WITH_ATTENTION, by:<human>, findings_sha:<design sha>} recorded AFTER Gate 1.5; a re-run producing a new design sha invalidates it.
Gate 2.5 remains the hard delivery rule (architect diff evidence for the change sha).

Gate 2 (HIL delivery approval) is mandatory before completed/closed/done: decision {gate:2, APPROVE|APPROVE_WITH_ATTENTION, by:<human>, findings_sha:<diff sha>} recorded AFTER Gate 2.5, with item.review_dispositions.diff having zero PENDING blocking findings.

Enforcement is deterministic/offline and fail-closed: gate1_transition_check (no grandfathering except config/gate-baseline.json entries with expiry) + gate2_completion_check, wired into precheck fast and ci-cd-gates; core.backlog.set_status refuses completion without Gate 2 unless force is enabled by PF_GATE_FORCE=1 plus an audited gate_override decision (CI/precheck always refuse force).
Both checkers support --report (dry-run, exit 0) and print structured allow/deny lines with reason codes; single predicate reuse (gate1_check.evaluate, architect_review.gate_view).
PENDING semantics are explicit: only PENDING blocks; ACTIONED/ACCEPTED/DEFERRED/REJECTED resolve, matching architect_review.pending_blocking.

Negative self-tests prove: missing design evidence fails, missing Gate 1 fails, stale approval (findings_sha mismatch) fails, missing Gate 2 fails, pending diff findings fail, force without PF_GATE_FORCE fails.
Docs (REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE) state the four gates are hard for every item, the decision schema, the fail-closed rules and the rollout baseline.
Language rule: these are build/CI gate tooling (not shipped product runtime), so Python is permitted; recorded in the item.

Design evidence sha = sha256(design body: objective/approach/in_scope/out_of_scope/ACs/components/files/risks/rollback)[:12]; diff sha = architect_review.diff_sha(). Evidence records the sha; gates recompute and compare.
Ordering predicate: a decision is valid only if decision.findings_sha == the current evidence sha AND decision.at >= evidence.at; otherwise STALE_APPROVAL.

Force audit sink: force requires PF_GATE_FORCE=1, PF_CI unset, and appends a gate_override decision (by/note/findings_sha) to the item; decisions are committed to git (append-only history). CI refuses overrides.
Baseline: config/gate-baseline.json entries require until (ISO date) + reason; expired/unknown entries DENY; baseline edits are ordinary reviewed changes (no hidden reopen).
Single predicate: set_status and gate2_completion_check both call core/gate_predicates.gate2_ready(); gate1_transition_check calls gate1_check.evaluate(). No duplicate PENDING logic.

Authorization/scope: decisions are recorded only by the HIL session through core.backlog.update (never auto-approved); needs_api=no; decision records are control-plane (non-tenant), findings stay reviewer-owned.
in_scope: Hard-gate the review lifecycle: Gate 1.5 -> Gate 1 before work, Gate 2.5 -> Gate 2 before completion
out_of_scope: Retroactive re-review of legacy items already completed before rollout (baseline records them; they are not re-opened).
Moving the gates to Go (tooling classification; revisit if enforcement moves into the runtime service).
Approver authentication/SSO (decision `by` is asserted by the HIL session, not cryptographically signed).
approach: Implement design_sha (design body) + evidence at; gate1_transition_check (reuse gate1_check.evaluate) requires design evidence + Gate 1 decision bound to design sha; gate2_completion_check + set_status share core/gate_predicates.gate2_ready (Gate 2.5 diff view, no PENDING, Gate 2 decision bound to diff sha, ordering); baseline with expiry; force only with PF_GATE_FORCE=1 and PF_CI unset; structured reason codes; self-tests (allow, deny x5, report, baseline expiry).
verification: Objective achieved: Hard-gate the review lifecycle: Gate 1.5 -> Gate 1 before work, Gate 2.5 -> Gate 2 before completion
risks: Legacy in-flight items fail when they next transition until a design review is run (mitigated by baseline + --report).
Force override misuse (mitigated by PF_GATE_FORCE + audited gate_override decision; CI refuses).
Approval replay after a re-review (mitigated by findings_sha binding).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing gate enforcement (core/e2e_lifecycle.py, core/merge_gate.py, /api/v1/engineering/gates) with a Go transition-guard: block new->in_progress without recorded Gate 1.5 findings dispositioned + Gate 1 approval; block in_progress->completed without Gate 2 approval + recorded HIL delivery approval. Enforce server-side at transition API (not UI-only).

dependency_findings.required_state: doD gate integrated at same close-guard

conflict_findings: BI-PF-1410 touches close/merge path; sequence with a single shared guard module to avoid divergent enforcement
BI-PF-1430 writes item gate fields; keep writes main-thread-owned (CL-002)
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1430 stores 1.5/2.5 findings on item+gate sheet - reuse its storage, don't add a second store
BI-PF-1410 adds DoD/verification-before-close - coordinate so both checks live in one close-guard
No existing item enforces new->in_progress ordering; this is the novel part
analysis.rationale: Lifecycle gates are bypassable because transitions are unvalidated; centralizing transition checks in the existing gate service closes the loophole without new infrastructure.
assumptions: Backlog item state machine is centralized (single writer) in e2e_lifecycle/backlog service
Gate 1.5/2.5 findings are persisted per BI-PF-1430 or can be queried now
HIL delivery approval has a defined approver role
risks: Breaking in-flight items stuck without Gate 1 approval
Operators may disable gate to unblock work - add audited override with alert
HIL approval source may be ambiguous for non-hardware items
evidence: Only Gate 2.5 is mechanically enforced today; items can go new->completed
Existing gate APIs (/api/v1/engineering/gates, /api/v1/gates/*) provide the enforcement surface
missing_info: Which role can perform a break-glass override, and is it audited+alerted?
Is HIL approval required for all items or only hardware-touching scope?
Backfill plan for existing new/completed items lacking Gate 1 evidence
